title: ComfortDelGro to offer cross-border taxi rides around the clock to JB from Nov 23, Singapore News

 singapore ComfortDelGro to offer cross-border taxi rides around the clock to JB from Nov 23
 It partners Malaysian platform Kummute to expand services between Singapore and JB. From Nov 23, Zig customers can book cross-border rides through the Zig app between seven days and four hours before their intended journey. PHOTO: AsiaOne/Fitri Salleh PUBLISHED ON November 17, 2026 2:39 PM BY Asyiqin Nadzri ComfortDelGro has partnered Malaysian ride-hailing platform Kummute to expand cross-border point-to-point transport services between Singapore and Johor Bahru (JB), from Nov 23.
 The partnership will allow rides booked through either platform to be fulfilled by vehicles from both networks, giving commuters access to a larger pool of vehicles for cross-border journeys. It will operate round the clock.
 In a press release on Tuesday (Nov 17), Zig by ComfortDelGro — a transport booking platform that brings together Singapore’s largest taxi fleet and a growing ride-hail service — said it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Kummute, operated by Malaysian company Kumpool Sdn Bhd, to enhance connectivity between the two cities.
 Bookings can also be made through Zig’s customer service hotline 6552-1111.
 The partnership comes as both companies join the enhanced Cross-Border Taxi Scheme as licensed ride-hail and e-hailing operators.
 Bookings available up to seven days in advance
 From Nov 23, Zig customers can book cross-border rides through the Zig app between seven days and four hours before their intended journey.
 Fixed fares will be displayed upfront, allowing passengers to know the cost of their trips before confirming their bookings. Customers can also make reservations via phone call.
 Pick-ups available across Singapore
 For trips from Singapore to Johor, passengers can be picked up from anywhere in Singapore and dropped off within a designated operating zone covering Johor Bahru, Skudai, Iskandar Puteri and Senai.
 For return journeys from Johor Bahru to Singapore, pick-ups will initially be available at four designated locations, with passengers able to be dropped off anywhere in Singapore.
 Wider point-to-point pick-up options in Johor Bahru will be introduced progressively, Zig said.
 Michael Huang, head of Singapore point-to-point mobility business at ComfortDelGro, said the partnership would make cross-border travel more accessible and convenient.
 "Through our partnership with Kummute, we are improving access to cross-border travel while making it easier for customers to plan and book their journeys, with upfront fixed fares and the flexibility of booking through the Zig app or our customer service hotline," he said.
 Lim Han Weng, director of Kumpool Sdn Bhd, said the partnership would expand transport options for the hundreds of thousands of people who cross the Causeway daily for work, studies, business and family visits.
 He added that combining the two companies' networks would strengthen connectivity between Singapore and Johor as the cities become increasingly connected.
